key_insight: Pretrained Softmax-attention Vision Transformers can be converted into efficient linear-attention models by combining architectural alignment with a short, targeted test-time training stage that closes the representational gap and enables direct weight reuse.
problem_solved: Bridges the incompatibility between Softmax attention and linear-complexity attention so practitioners can reuse expensive pretrained ViT weights rather than training linear-attention models from scratch, overcoming the quadratic attention bottleneck without prohibitive compute.
method: Architectural alignment: introduce lightweight compatibility adapters and design linear-attention modules to mimic the functional behaviour of Softmax attention so pretrained weights are more directly transferable.

Test-time training (TTT): apply a brief, self-supervised calibration step on target data (e.g., layer-matching / consistency objectives) to adapt pretrained parameters to the linearized attention dynamics.
Low-overhead deployment: keep additional parameters and adaptation steps minimal to preserve linear inference complexity and practical efficiency gains.
impact: Enables practical deployment of compute- and memory-efficient Vision Transformers by leveraging existing pretrained models instead of costly retraining, lowering barriers for high-resolution and long-sequence vision applications.

paper_title: Linearizing Vision Transformer with Test-Time Training
